opening_message:
Ticket 1: Karen Black (employee ID E008) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E008.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Karen Black (E008) is a full-time Payroll Specialist requesting admin access to Source Code. As a full-time employee, maximum is write unless her role owns the system; Source Code is owned by Engineer, not Payroll Specialist, so admin is not permitted. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security record for Karen Black (E008): contractor with basic security training. Contractors cannot be granted admin, and write requires advanced training, so maximum level is read. Requested admin to Source Code; recommend granting read.
reason: Karen Black (E008) requested admin to Source Code. Admin is not permitted: per HR she is full-time but her role (Payroll Specialist) does not own Source Code (owned by Engineer), capping her at write; per Security she is a contractor with basic training, for whom write requires advanced training and admin is never allowed, capping her at read. Given the conflicting employment records, I grant the safe maximum that is permissible under the more restrictive interpretation: read.

1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if role owns the system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

Role: Payroll Specialist, does not own Source Code (Engineer owns it).

Requested: admin.

- If contractor: max is read (basic training, no advanced). Granted = read.
